turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We planned a barbecue on Saturday, but now they're saying rain in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's annoying. You could move it to the morning, or keep the time and set up a canopy. What do you think?

contexts.pending: move the barbecue earlier or keep it and use a canopy
think_reask: So, for the barbecue, earlier in the day or a canopy?
Okay, have you decided? Move it to the morning or stick it out under a canopy?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were working out what to do about Saturday's barbecue and the rain.
Hi again. Any decision on the barbecue, earlier start or canopy?

endings.user: Let's move it to late morning. Brunch barbecue!
endings.moshi: Love it. Send a quick message to everyone today so they can plan around it.

endings.user: We'll keep the time and borrow my neighbor's canopy.
endings.moshi: Good plan. Set it up early and stake it down well in case the wind picks up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's supposed to be really hot tomorrow.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: How hot are we talking?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Close to a hundred, and I promised the kids an outing.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then maybe the pool, or somewhere indoors like a museum. Which would they enjoy more?

contexts.pending: pool or an indoor outing on a hot day
think_reask: So, pool day or a cool museum for the kids tomorrow?
Alright, which outing sounds better for the heat, the pool or indoors?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing between the pool and an indoor outing for the hot day.
There you are. Still deciding what to do with the kids in the heat?

endings.user: The pool, for sure. They'd never forgive me otherwise.
endings.moshi: Go in the morning before it gets crowded, and bring lots of sunscreen and water.

endings.user: Museum. My youngest burns way too easily.
endings.moshi: Sensible. Many museums have kids' areas, and you'll all stay nice and cool.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a snowstorm coming Thursday night and I'm supposed to drive to my sister's on Friday.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That could make the roads rough. Would you rather leave Thursday afternoon before it hits, or wait and go Saturday?

contexts.pending: leave before the storm or wait until Saturday
think_reask: So, are you leaving early on Thursday or holding off until Saturday?
Time's up. What's the plan for the drive to your sister's?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were deciding whether you beat the storm Thursday or wait until Saturday.
Hi again. Any thoughts on when to drive to your sister's?

endings.user: I'll leave Thursday right after lunch.
endings.moshi: Good idea. Fill up the tank and pack a blanket and snacks, just in case traffic slows down.

endings.user: Saturday. I don't want to rush.
endings.moshi: That's the safer choice. Give the plows a day to clear things and check the road conditions before you go.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, did you see the forecast for tomorrow?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Yeah, thunderstorms after three.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh. Do you still want to do the hike?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: We could start really early and be down by noon.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How early is really early?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Like leave the house at six.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fine, but you're making the coffee.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should we bring the patio chairs inside? It's getting really windy.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Probably. One of them blew into the fence last time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, I forgot about that. Can you grab the cushions?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure. Where do you want them, the garage?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, on the shelf by the bikes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, is it still raining out there?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Just drizzling now. The sky looks lighter over the hills.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do you think it'll clear up in time for the market?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Maybe. If not, we can just take umbrellas. It's only a ten minute walk.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: True. I really want those peaches before they sell out.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Then let's not wait too long. Grab your jacket.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm painting the fence this week. What weather do I need for that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ideally a dry day that's mild, not too hot and not freezing. Most paints also need a few hours without rain after you finish.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What if it rains the next day?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Usually that's fine. Check the can, many exterior paints are rain resistant after a few hours of drying.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And is direct sun bad? The fence gets / pretty much full sun all afternoon.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Strong sun can make paint dry too fast and leave marks. Paint that side in the morning while it's still shaded.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Morning works. Wednesday looks dry so far.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then Wednesday morning it is. Just wait until any dew on the wood has dried off before you start.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What should I pack for a weekend where it might be sunny or might pour?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Layers are your friend. A t-shirt, a warm sweater and a light waterproof jacket cover most situations.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about shoes? I only want to bring one pair.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then pick something comfortable that can handle getting wet, like trail runners or water resistant sneakers.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I bother with an umbrella or / is the jacket enough?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If the jacket has a hood, it's usually enough. A small folding umbrella is nice if you'll be walking around a city.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We'll be in a city, mostly.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then toss the umbrella in your bag. It barely takes up any space.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My running club meets outside at six in the morning. It's going to be below freezing all week.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Running in the cold is fine with the right gear. Wear a base layer that wicks sweat, plus gloves and a hat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I always feel freezing for the first ten minutes.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's normal. Dress as if it's about ten degrees warmer than it is, because you'll heat up quickly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about ice on the paths?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the real risk. Shorten your stride, slow down on corners, and consider slip-on traction cleats.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe I'll just / no, I'll still go, I don't want to lose my streak.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good for you. Just warm up indoors for a few minutes first so your muscles aren't cold.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it a good idea to plant tomatoes this weekend? It's been warm.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It depends on the nights. Tomatoes don't like it when nights drop much below fifty degrees.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The forecast says one more cold night next Tuesday.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then you could plant them and cover them that night with a sheet or a bucket. Or just wait a week.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm impatient, I want to plant them now / but I don't want to lose them.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Plant them now and set a reminder for Tuesday evening to cover them. That's a fair compromise.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would an old blanket work?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, just take it off in the morning so the plants get light and don't overheat.

option_sets.lead_in: It might rain on Saturday and we need to pick a plan for the kids.
options: The first idea is the zoo, which is fun but mostly outdoors.
Then there's the science museum, all indoors, but it gets really crowded on rainy days.
And the last one is staying in with a fort, board games and a movie marathon.
moshi_comment: The science museum is safe from the rain, but expect crowds since everyone else will have the same idea. The zoo could be great if the rain holds off, and it might even be quieter. Staying in is cozy and cheap, but kids can get restless.
How old are the kids, and how much do they mind getting a bit wet? If they're fine in raincoats, the zoo might be surprisingly fun. Otherwise, go early to the museum to beat the crowds.

option_sets.lead_in: There's a heat wave coming and I'm trying to figure out what to do on my day off.
options: One option is going to the lake, but it's an hour drive and the beach has no shade.
Another is spending the afternoon at the mall, which is boring but at least air conditioned.
Option three is going to the public pool in the morning before it gets too hot.
And the last one is staying home with the fan on and catching up on my shows.
moshi_comment: The morning pool trip sounds smart, you get to swim and you're home before the worst of the heat. The lake is lovely, but no shade in a heat wave can be rough. The mall is a fine backup if you need to cool off in the afternoon.
Do you have a beach umbrella? If you do, the lake could be great. If not, I'd do the pool in the morning and then relax at home with your shows.
